title: 2024 AMC 10A Problem 17
statement: Two teams are in a best-two-out-of-three playoff: the teams will play at most \(3\) games, and the winner of the playoff is the first team to win \(2\) games. The first game is played on Team A’s home field, and the remaining games are played on Team B’s home field. Team A has a \(\tfrac23\) chance of winning at home, and its probability of winning when playing away from home is \(p.\) Outcomes of the games are independent. The probability that Team A wins the playoff is \(\tfrac12.\) Then \(p\) can be written in the form \(\tfrac12\!\left(m - \sqrt{n}\right),\) where \(m\) and \(n\) are positive integers. What is \(m + n?\)

solutions.text: Team A takes game \(1\) at home with probability \(\tfrac23,\) and each away game with probability \(p.\) It can win the playoff three disjoint ways: win games \(1, 2;\) win \(1,\) lose \(2,\) win \(3;\) lose \(1,\) win \(2, 3.\) Adding those, \(\tfrac23 p + \tfrac23(1 - p)p + \tfrac13 p^2 = \tfrac12.\) This cleans up to \(2p^2 - 8p + 3 = 0,\) so \(p = \tfrac{4 - \sqrt{10}}{2} = \tfrac12\!\left(4 - \sqrt{10}\right).\) Then \(m = 4,\) \(n = 10,\) and \(m + n = 14.\) Thus, E is the correct answer.
hints: List the ways Team A wins two games: win games \(1\) and \(2;\) win \(1,\) lose \(2,\) win \(3;\) lose \(1,\) win \(2,\) win \(3\)
Set the total probability equal to \(\tfrac12\) and solve the resulting quadratic in \(p\)
